name: Odoo Community
summary: A broad modular business suite spanning finance, sales, inventory, purchasing, manufacturing, and more.
problem: Replaces disconnected back-office tools with a configurable suite and shared operational data.
idealFor: Organizations that want a modular ERP platform and have an implementation partner or internal technical team.
editionBoundary: Community modules are LGPL; Odoo Enterprise modules use a separate proprietary license.

name: ERPNext
summary: A full ERP for accounting, procurement, stock, manufacturing, projects, CRM, and service operations.
problem: Gives growing companies one auditable system for finance and operational workflows without per-module licensing.
idealFor: SMBs and mid-market organizations that value flexible workflows and a strong services ecosystem.

name: Dolibarr
summary: A long-running ERP and CRM for invoicing, accounting, orders, suppliers, inventory, and projects.
problem: Provides approachable business administration for companies that need useful modules without a heavyweight ERP program.
idealFor: Small and mid-sized companies, associations, and regional service businesses.

name: Bigcapital
summary: Modern double-entry accounting and inventory for small and medium businesses.
problem: Centralizes invoices, bills, expenses, inventory, and financial statements in a modern web application.
idealFor: SMBs seeking an extensible QuickBooks or Xero-style accounting system.

name: Frappe Books
summary: Offline-friendly desktop accounting with invoicing, double-entry books, and financial reports.
problem: Gives small businesses a focused accounting application that can operate locally without a complex server estate.
idealFor: Small companies and finance teams that prefer desktop-first, offline-capable bookkeeping.

name: Lago
summary: API-first metering and usage-based billing for complex subscription pricing.
problem: Separates billing logic from product code and supports subscriptions, usage, credits, and invoicing.
idealFor: SaaS and platform businesses with evolving or consumption-based pricing.

name: Kill Bill
summary: Mature subscription billing and payments infrastructure designed for extensibility and scale.
problem: Handles complex catalogs, subscriptions, invoices, payments, entitlements, and billing plugins.
idealFor: Mid-market and enterprise subscription businesses with demanding billing requirements.

name: Frappe HR
summary: HR and payroll covering employee records, recruitment, attendance, leave, performance, and payroll.
problem: Connects the employee lifecycle to structured approvals and operational HR workflows.
idealFor: Growing companies that want an extensible HRIS and can localize payroll rules.

name: OrangeHRM
summary: A long-established HR management system for employee data, leave, time, and core HR processes.
problem: Standardizes essential people operations for organizations moving away from spreadsheets.
idealFor: SMBs wanting a recognizable HRIS with an established implementation market.
editionBoundary: The Starter application is GPL; advanced paid modules and services are separate.

name: Horilla
summary: A modern Django HRMS with recruitment, onboarding, attendance, payroll, performance, and assets.
problem: Brings broad HR workflows into one customizable web platform.
idealFor: SMBs seeking a modern interface and Python-based customization path.

name: OpenCATS
summary: A focused applicant tracking system and recruitment CRM for internal and agency hiring teams.
problem: Replaces inbox-and-spreadsheet recruiting with candidate records, job pipelines, and search.
idealFor: Budget-conscious recruiting teams that need a focused, established ATS.
editionBoundary: Modern OpenCATS code is MPL 2.0; inherited legacy CATS Project code carries its historical license and should be reviewed before redistribution.

name: Kimai
summary: Multi-user time tracking with teams, projects, approvals, reporting, exports, and invoicing.
problem: Creates reliable timesheet and utilization data for payroll, billing, and project control.
idealFor: Professional services, agencies, consultancies, and internal project teams.

name: Documenso
summary: A modern self-hostable platform for preparing, sending, and signing digital documents.
problem: Keeps document-signing workflows and audit data under organizational control.
idealFor: HR, legal, sales, and operations teams replacing proprietary e-signature subscriptions.
editionBoundary: Community code is AGPL; commercial plans and enterprise services are offered separately.

name: Moodle
summary: The established learning management platform for courses, assessment, credentials, and learning ecosystems.
problem: Delivers structured training at scale while retaining control of learning data and integrations.
idealFor: Enterprises, education providers, public bodies, and regulated training programs.

name: Twenty
summary: A modern, extensible CRM designed as an open alternative to Salesforce.
problem: Gives technical revenue teams a flexible data model, workflows, and clean pipeline experience.
idealFor: Product-led and technical organizations that want to tailor CRM objects and automation.

name: SuiteCRM
summary: A mature CRM covering accounts, leads, opportunities, quotes, campaigns, workflows, and service cases.
problem: Provides deep traditional CRM functionality without enterprise seat licensing.
idealFor: Mid-market sales organizations needing rich CRM modules and partner-led customization.

name: EspoCRM
summary: A fast, customizable CRM with sales automation, email, calendars, workflows, and a REST API.
problem: Creates a practical 360-degree customer view without a complex enterprise CRM rollout.
idealFor: SMBs and mid-market teams that want a focused CRM and PHP customization ecosystem.

name: Frappe CRM
summary: A clean, modern CRM built on the extensible Frappe framework.
problem: Provides lightweight lead and deal management that can be adapted to specific sales processes.
idealFor: SMBs already using Frappe or wanting a customizable open CRM.

name: Easy!Appointments
summary: A self-hosted appointment scheduler with services, providers, availability, and calendar synchronization.
problem: Lets customers book available time without manual email coordination or per-seat scheduling fees.
idealFor: Service businesses, clinics, consultancies, and customer-facing sales teams.

name: Chatwoot
summary: Omnichannel customer support across live chat, email, social, messaging, and a help center.
problem: Unifies fragmented customer conversations and contact context into a collaborative support workspace.
idealFor: Digital businesses replacing Intercom, Zendesk, or scattered shared inboxes.
editionBoundary: The community application is MIT; paid cloud and enterprise capabilities are separate offerings.

name: Zammad
summary: A polished service desk with email, chat, phone, knowledge base, SLAs, and automation.
problem: Provides structured, auditable ticket handling across channels for support and internal service teams.
idealFor: Support desks and IT service teams that need mature workflows and a strong operator UI.

name: FreeScout
summary: A lightweight help desk and shared mailbox inspired by Help Scout.
problem: Turns shared support email into assignable, searchable conversations with team context.
idealFor: Small support teams that want simple deployment and familiar email workflows.

name: BookStack
summary: An approachable wiki organized around shelves, books, chapters, and pages.
problem: Makes internal and customer-facing knowledge easy to structure, own, search, and maintain.
idealFor: Teams that want an opinionated, user-friendly knowledge base with simple administration.

name: Fider
summary: A public feedback portal for collecting ideas, voting, discussion, and status updates.
problem: Creates a transparent, prioritized customer-feedback loop outside support tickets and spreadsheets.
idealFor: Product and customer-success teams that need an open alternative to proprietary feedback boards.

name: Mautic
summary: A comprehensive marketing automation platform for contacts, segments, campaigns, scoring, email, and journeys.
problem: Brings lead nurturing and campaign automation under the company's data and infrastructure control.
idealFor: B2B and lifecycle marketing teams with implementation and deliverability expertise.

name: listmonk
summary: A high-performance newsletter and mailing-list manager delivered as a compact self-hosted application.
problem: Sends high-volume campaigns and manages subscribers without paying a platform tax on every contact.
idealFor: Technical marketing teams that already control their SMTP or transactional email provider.

name: Ghost
summary: A modern publishing and membership platform for websites, newsletters, and subscriptions.
problem: Combines fast editorial publishing, audience ownership, memberships, and email distribution.
idealFor: Content-led businesses, publishers, thought-leadership teams, and membership products.

name: Strapi Community
summary: A popular headless CMS with customizable content types, APIs, roles, and a large plugin ecosystem.
problem: Gives marketing and engineering teams a shared content backend for websites, apps, and digital products.
idealFor: Digital teams that want API-first content management and JavaScript extensibility.
editionBoundary: The community core is MIT; enterprise features and cloud services are separately licensed.

name: Postiz
summary: A modern social media scheduling and publishing platform with collaborative workflows.
problem: Centralizes planning and publishing across social channels in a self-hostable workspace.
idealFor: Marketing teams and agencies replacing proprietary social scheduling suites.

name: Matomo
summary: A mature privacy-oriented web analytics platform with traffic, goals, campaigns, and reporting.
problem: Provides Google Analytics-style insight while retaining first-party control of visitor data.
idealFor: Organizations with privacy, compliance, or data-residency requirements.

name: Plausible Analytics
summary: A lightweight, privacy-focused web analytics product with a deliberately simple reporting experience.
problem: Makes essential website analytics understandable while reducing cookie and tracking complexity.
idealFor: Marketing teams that want clear, privacy-friendly website metrics rather than a large analytics suite.

name: PostHog FOSS
summary: An open product-analytics stack for events, funnels, retention, feature flags, experiments, and session replay.
problem: Connects product behavior to experimentation and delivery in a single technical platform.
idealFor: Software companies with engineering support and sophisticated product analytics needs.
editionBoundary: This profile points to the FOSS-only repository; PostHog's main monorepo also contains separately licensed enterprise code.

name: Metabase OSS
summary: Approachable business intelligence for questions, dashboards, SQL, alerts, and embedded analytics.
problem: Lets non-technical teams answer recurring data questions without waiting for bespoke analyst reports.
idealFor: SMBs through enterprises seeking fast self-service BI and straightforward deployment.
editionBoundary: The open-source edition is AGPL; commercial Metabase editions have a separate license.

name: Apache Superset
summary: An enterprise-scale data exploration and visualization platform with rich dashboards and SQL tooling.
problem: Serves many analytical users and data sources through a scalable, extensible BI layer.
idealFor: Data-mature mid-market and enterprise organizations with platform engineering capacity.

name: Redash
summary: A well-known SQL-first query, visualization, dashboard, and alerting tool.
problem: Gives analysts a simple shared home for database queries and lightweight dashboards.
idealFor: Technical analytics teams that prefer direct SQL workflows and a compact BI surface.

name: Lightdash
summary: A dbt-native BI layer for governed metrics, self-service exploration, and analytics as code.
problem: Turns dbt models into consistent business metrics without duplicating semantic logic in dashboards.
idealFor: Modern data teams already standardized on dbt and software-style analytics workflows.
editionBoundary: The open-source core is MIT; the repository contains a separately licensed enterprise directory.

name: Apache Airflow
summary: The established platform for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring data workflows as code.
problem: Makes complex batch data pipelines maintainable, observable, versioned, and recoverable.
idealFor: Data engineering organizations with Python skills and production orchestration needs.

name: Meltano
summary: A declarative, code-first data-integration engine with a broad Singer connector ecosystem.
problem: Standardizes extraction and loading projects while keeping pipeline configuration version-controlled.
idealFor: Lean data teams that prefer composable tooling and code-first deployment.

name: OpenMetadata
summary: An integrated metadata, discovery, lineage, quality, observability, and governance platform.
problem: Creates trusted context around enterprise data so people and systems can discover and govern it.
idealFor: Data-platform teams formalizing ownership, lineage, quality, and AI-ready data context.

name: DataHub
summary: A scalable metadata platform for discovery, lineage, ownership, governance, and data products.
problem: Makes a complex data estate searchable and understandable with continuously ingested metadata.
idealFor: Large data organizations needing a developer-friendly, extensible catalog and metadata graph.

name: ClickHouse
summary: A high-performance column-oriented database for real-time analytics and large-scale reporting.
problem: Runs fast analytical queries across very large event and operational datasets at efficient cost.
idealFor: Engineering and data teams building observability, product analytics, or real-time BI platforms.

name: InvenTree
summary: A modern inventory and part-management system with stock, purchasing, builds, BOMs, and APIs.
problem: Creates accurate parts and stock control for product, manufacturing, and technical operations.
idealFor: Hardware teams, manufacturers, labs, and technical inventory operations.

name: OpenBoxes
summary: A mature supply-chain and inventory system shaped by healthcare and humanitarian logistics.
problem: Tracks inventory, stock movements, shipments, purchasing, and replenishment across facilities.
idealFor: Healthcare, NGOs, multi-site logistics, and operations with traceable stock flows.

name: Snipe-IT
summary: A focused IT asset and software-license management system with assignments and lifecycle history.
problem: Answers who has each asset, where it is, what it cost, and when it must be renewed or replaced.
idealFor: IT and operations teams that need a dependable ITAM register without a full ITSM rollout.

name: GLPI
summary: A broad IT management suite combining service desk, assets, licenses, CMDB, contracts, and data-center records.
problem: Unifies IT service and asset processes with auditable lifecycle and support records.
idealFor: Mid-sized and enterprise IT teams wanting an extensible ITSM and ITAM platform.

name: Paperless-ngx
summary: A searchable document archive with ingestion, OCR, tagging, correspondents, document types, and workflows.
problem: Turns scanned and digital documents into a searchable, categorized operational archive.
idealFor: Back offices and document-heavy teams that need private OCR and retention workflows.

name: NetBox
summary: The established source of truth for networks, IPAM, data centers, devices, circuits, and infrastructure automation.
problem: Replaces network spreadsheets with a structured model and API that can drive automation.
idealFor: Infrastructure and network teams operating non-trivial on-premise or hybrid estates.

name: Keycloak
summary: Enterprise identity and access management with SSO, OIDC, SAML, federation, MFA, and fine-grained authorization.
problem: Centralizes application authentication and access policy instead of rebuilding identity in every system.
idealFor: Organizations standardizing workforce or customer identity across many applications.

name: authentik Community
summary: A flexible identity provider and authentication layer with modern flows, federation, and application proxies.
problem: Adds SSO and policy to internal or customer applications with a modern administrative experience.
idealFor: Technical IT teams seeking an approachable identity platform and reverse-proxy integration.
editionBoundary: Core code is MIT; the authentik/enterprise directory is separately licensed.

name: Grafana OSS
summary: The ubiquitous visualization and observability interface for metrics, logs, traces, and operational data.
problem: Creates shared dashboards and alerting across heterogeneous infrastructure and application data sources.
idealFor: Any technical organization operating production systems and shared observability practices.
editionBoundary: Grafana OSS is AGPL; enterprise plugins and services are separately licensed.

name: Prometheus
summary: The cloud-native standard for time-series metrics collection, querying, alerting, and service monitoring.
problem: Provides reliable numerical telemetry and alert rules for dynamic infrastructure and applications.
idealFor: Engineering organizations building cloud-native or infrastructure monitoring platforms.

name: SigNoz Community
summary: An OpenTelemetry-native observability platform unifying logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, and alerts.
problem: Provides a coherent self-hosted alternative to commercial APM and observability suites.
idealFor: Engineering teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry and wanting one operational interface.
editionBoundary: The community platform is open source; enterprise features and managed cloud are separate.

name: Wazuh
summary: An open security platform for endpoint monitoring, threat detection, log analysis, vulnerability data, and compliance.
problem: Consolidates endpoint and security telemetry into actionable detection and compliance workflows.
idealFor: Security teams building a cost-conscious SIEM/XDR and compliance monitoring capability.

name: Gitea
summary: A fast, lightweight software-development service for Git hosting, reviews, issues, packages, and actions.
problem: Provides private source control and collaboration with modest infrastructure requirements.
idealFor: SMBs, internal engineering groups, and regulated teams wanting simple self-hosted Git services.

name: Jenkins
summary: The established automation server with an enormous plugin ecosystem for CI/CD and operational workflows.
problem: Automates repeatable software build, test, release, and infrastructure processes across diverse stacks.
idealFor: Organizations with heterogeneous delivery tooling or substantial existing Jenkins expertise.

name: Rocket.Chat
summary: A large-scale communications platform for channels, direct messaging, federation, apps, and omnichannel workflows.
problem: Keeps mission-critical team and customer communication within controlled infrastructure.
idealFor: Organizations needing extensible, self-hosted real-time communication and integrations.
editionBoundary: Community code is open source; paid enterprise capabilities and services are separate.

name: Mattermost Community
summary: Secure collaboration for technical and operational teams, including messaging, playbooks, and workflow integrations.
problem: Supports sensitive team coordination and incident work where data control and extensibility matter.
idealFor: Engineering, operations, public sector, and regulated organizations.
editionBoundary: Community source is AGPL with documented exceptions; enterprise features use a commercial license.

name: OpenProject
summary: Comprehensive project management with planning, agile boards, roadmaps, time, budgets, meetings, and documentation.
problem: Gives management one auditable environment for traditional, agile, and hybrid project delivery.
idealFor: Professional services, public bodies, construction, product teams, and PMOs.
editionBoundary: Community Edition is GPL; enterprise add-ons and support are separate.

name: Plane Community
summary: A modern work-management platform for issues, cycles, modules, roadmaps, pages, and product delivery.
problem: Provides a contemporary open alternative to Jira, Linear, Monday, and ClickUp.
idealFor: Product and engineering teams that prioritize modern UX and self-hosting.
editionBoundary: The Community Edition is AGPL; paid tiers and enterprise features are separate.

name: Leantime
summary: Goals-focused project management designed for non-project managers and neurodiverse teams.
problem: Connects strategy, goals, projects, tasks, time, and retrospectives in an approachable workspace.
idealFor: SMBs, innovation teams, and organizations needing accessible planning and execution.
editionBoundary: Core is AGPL; some plugins may use separate enterprise licenses.

name: Nextcloud
summary: A private collaboration cloud for files, sharing, calendars, contacts, communication, and an extensive app ecosystem.
problem: Gives organizations control of collaborative data while replacing multiple proprietary workspace services.
idealFor: Any organization prioritizing data sovereignty, private collaboration, and extensibility.

name: Wiki.js
summary: A modern, extensible wiki with a polished editor, authentication integrations, search, and multiple storage options.
problem: Creates a flexible home for technical and organizational knowledge with enterprise authentication options.
idealFor: Technical teams that want a modern Node-based wiki and broad integration choices.

name: Jitsi Meet
summary: A widely deployed secure video-conferencing platform for web and mobile meetings.
problem: Provides private virtual meetings without requiring every participant to use a proprietary conferencing account.
idealFor: Organizations, public bodies, service providers, and communities needing controlled video meetings.
